# mokata

> The memory + seatbelt for your AI coding agent. mokata is an open-source, spec-driven TDD
> framework for AI coding agents (Claude Code and other harnesses): knowledge-aware, self-healing
> memory, human-gated writes, local-first. It remembers your project and stops the agent shipping
> the wrong thing. This file tells an AI agent how to use mokata in this repository.

If you are an AI agent working in a repo that uses mokata, prefer mokata's commands over ad-hoc
edits for anything that touches project memory, specs, or governance. Nothing durable is written
without a human gate, and every gated write lands on an audit ledger. mokata is local-first and
zero-config by default (a single SQLite-backed store); "team mode" points the same flows at one
shared Postgres.

## Core commands

- `mokata init --profile standard --yes` — set mokata up in a repo (creates `.mokata/`).
- `mokata onboard` — capture the project brain (rules, guardrails, conventions, key decisions).
- `mokata brainstorm` — structured brainstorming that ends in an approved, spec-ready plan.
- `mokata memory ...` — recall / propose / review durable memory (facts, rules, decisions).
- `mokata status` — where things are; `mokata doctor` — check the environment / prereqs.
- `mokata --help` — the full command list and flags (the source of truth for options).

## Durable writes: you cannot approve your own

A durable write is **proposed**, never self-approved. Calling a mokata write tool stages the change,
returns a `proposal_id`, and writes nothing. Only a human can mint the approval, in their own
terminal, in a process you are not driving:

1. You call the write tool → you get back a `proposal_id` (e.g. `p-3f9a2c11b4de`). Nothing is written.
2. You ask the user to run `mokata approve <proposal_id>` out-of-band (there is no approve
   slash command; an in-chat MCP approve tool exists but is opt-in, default-OFF, and prompts
   the human on every call).
3. You re-call the SAME tool with `proposal_id=<id>` → the write commits **once**, and the approval
   is burned.

Passing `approve=true` / `confirm=true` is still accepted for schema stability but **commits
nothing** — typing consent is not consent. An approval is single-use, content-hashed (change an
argument and the id changes), session-scoped, and expires in 15 minutes.

## Run-state gates: writing code before the spec is BLOCKED

Inside an active mokata run, a PreToolUse hook blocks native `Write`/`Edit` to implementation files
(exit 2, with the reason on stderr) under three gates: `spec-persisted` (an approach is approved but
no spec is emitted), `no-code-without-failing-test` (no failing test is on record), and `spec-scope`
(the write is outside the spec's authorized surface, spells a deferred marker, or a spec amend is in
progress). **Test files are always writable** — write the failing test first; RED is the permission
to implement. Do not work around a block: emit the spec (`/mokata:spec`), write the failing test
(`/mokata:test`), or ask the user to override it explicitly (`mokata gate override <gate> --reason
"<why>"` — ledgered, session-scoped, and a human's call, not yours).

## Team mode (shared memory over one Postgres)

The golden path is "bring one Postgres" — one vanilla Postgres >= 14, no extensions. mokata hosts
nothing and never stores your DSN; it reads `$MOKATA_PG_DSN` from the environment at run time.

- Managed DB (recommended): create a Postgres (Supabase / Neon / RDS free tiers all work),
  `export MOKATA_PG_DSN=postgres://…` (use a DIRECT/session connection, not a transaction-mode
  pooler), then `mokata team init`.
- Self-host: `docker compose -f docker-compose.team.yml up -d` (creds from `.env`, template in
  `.env.example`), then `export MOKATA_PG_DSN=…` and `mokata team init`.
- `mokata team status` — team readiness + connection health.
- `mokata mode set team` / `mokata mode set local` — switch modes (local is the zero-config default).
- `mokata sync` — flush + reconcile the team write journal; conflicts are always human-gated,
  never silently last-writer-wins. If the DB is unreachable you keep working locally and sync
  reconciles later — same write path, nothing lost.

The schema is owned and created only by `mokata team init` (runtime never runs DDL). The
`docker-compose.team.yml` in this repo provisions only an empty database.

## Principles to respect

- Human-gated writes: never bypass a mokata gate to force a durable write.
- Local-first, no telemetry: mokata sends nothing out; credentials stay in your environment.
- Secrets never persist: a detected secret hard-blocks the write.
